# Osprey (01, architect) — SPD-096

## Brief
Settle the design of a parked bucket for the board, and write it down as a design
note the engineer on this ticket will build from. You decide; you do not implement.
No code changes, no CLI changes, no `.base` changes — a document only.

## The problem

Read `ledger/tickets/SPD-096.md` for the full statement. In short: ticket status is
`queued|active|done|declined`, `queued` is a 46-deep backlog, and priority is the only
sort inside it. A ticket that is genuinely important but deliberately not-now has
nowhere to go but a priority that lies about it. On 2026-09-16 Eric parked six BadTakes
tickets by tagging them (`deferred` on BAD-040, BAD-041, BAD-042, BAD-043, BAD-048;
`waiting` on BAD-021). Nothing reads those tags, so `spud board` still opens with the
four P1 splits every session, and the `SessionStart` hook still injects them.

## The three questions, in order

1. **Tag or status.** A fifth ticket status (`deferred`) makes the state machine enforce
   parking and puts it in every rendered note and Bases view for free; it costs a
   migration, new legal transitions, and hook/render/board changes. A tag costs nothing
   structural but is enforced by nobody and must be read explicitly everywhere it
   matters. Pick one and say why, in terms of what actually goes wrong under each in six
   months. This is the expensive-if-wrong half — a fifth status is hard to walk back.
2. **What the board does by default.** Hide parked tickets behind a flag (`--all`), sort
   them last regardless of priority, or group them under their own heading. Whatever you
   choose must also hold for `spud board --brief`, which the `SessionStart` hook injects
   — that injection is the surface that actually nags, and SPD-048 (queued) already wants
   that context smaller. Say what `spud board`, `spud board --brief` and the hook
   injection each print, concretely, with a sketch of the output.
3. **Whether `waiting` differs from `deferred`.** Waiting on an external event (BAD-021
   waits on App Store approval) resolves on its own and is worth resurfacing when it
   might have resolved; deferred is a choice and is not. Decide whether that difference
   earns a second mechanism, one mechanism with a reason field, or nothing at all.

  and what stops it from silently rotting the way it just did.

- Rendered ticket notes carry the status in frontmatter. Say what a parked ticket's

- `spud board --help` must document how to see parked tickets. Draft that line.
- The six tickets above must read correctly under your mechanism. Say what each becomes.

## Result
Produced docs/design/2026-09-16-parked-tickets.md (405 lines): the decision up front, why (tag vs status in six-month failure terms; waiting vs deferred), what spud board, board --brief, the SessionStart injection and board --parked print with output sketches, the exact DDL_0003 and v_board SQL, every transition and the ticket move contract, the parked frontmatter, the Board.base YAML for Spud to paste, the drafted board --help, an ordered implementation checklist naming files, line numbers and the tests to extend, Spud's edits and the rollout, the six tickets' commands, and nine accepted risks. Decision in three sentences: parked is a fifth ticket status (migration 0003_parked rebuilds tickets with status IN queued|active|parked|done|declined plus parked_reason and parked_until columns, CHECK-bound so a reason exists iff parked), set only by ticket move --status parked --reason … [--until YYYY-MM-DD] and cleared by a move to queued|active|declined, with parked->parked as a renewal. Waiting is not a second status: it is parked with an --until date, the only difference the board can act on; the brief board and the SessionStart injection omit parked tickets except one trailing count line and one full line for each whose date has arrived, placed above the queued block so a future cap keeps it, while the full board sorts them after queued and board --parked lists them with reason and date. Verified by a scratch sqlite3 probe on the real DDL (sqlite 3.53.4): the rebuild needs foreign keys off before BEGIN and v_board/v_fleet dropped before the rename, foreign_key_check is clean, every CHECK holds, and CREATE VIEW tolerates a not-yet-existing column; the rollout hazard that the home's PreToolUse fails closed between merge and migrate is named, with the one-line merge-and-migrate answer. Left: the engineer builds it; Spud pastes the Board.base YAML, edits Home.md, the ticket template, CLAUDE.md and SPD-082's brief (its migration becomes 0004), runs the twelve commands for the six tickets, and confirms BAD-021's review date (2026-10-16 proposed) with Eric. No proposals filed.

## Outcome
Accepted whole. A fifth status is the right call: the tag failed the same week it was set because ticket edit --tag replaces the list and nothing validates it, and 'active plus deferred' is representable under a tag but not under a status. Folding waiting into parked --until is the sharper half of the decision — a date is the only part of 'waiting' the ledger can act on, and a second status would have recorded a difference it could never use. The sqlite3 probe on the real DDL and the fails-closed rollout hazard are why this was worth a fable.
